evidence.claim: SR 172 provides the approach from I-11/US 93, passing the turnoff for the Lakeview scenic viewpoint before its designation ends just short of the dam reservation’s security checkpoint.
evidence.quote: Shortly after passing the turnoff for the Lakeview scenic viewpoint, the SR 172 designation ends 1.61 miles (2.59 km) west of the Arizona state line, just prior to a security checkpoint at the boundary with the Bureau of Reclamation's Hoover Dam Reservation.

evidence.claim: SR 172 provides the approach from I-11/US 93, passing the turnoff for the Lakeview scenic viewpoint before its designation ends just short of the dam reservation’s security checkpoint.

evidence.claim: The entire state route lies within Lake Mead National Recreation Area, whose protected landscape includes the reservoir and surrounding desert terrain.
evidence.quote: The entire route is in Lake Mead National Recreation Area, Clark County.

evidence.claim: whose protected landscape includes the reservoir and surrounding desert terrain.
evidence.quote: It includes all of the eponymous Lake Mead as well as the smaller Lake Mohave – reservoirs on the river created by Hoover Dam and Davis Dam, respectively – and the surrounding desert terrain and wilderness.

evidence.claim: The dam’s crest once carried US 93 across the Colorado River.
evidence.quote: The heavily traveled U.S. Route 93 (US 93) ran along the dam's crest until October 2010, when the Hoover Dam Bypass opened.

evidence.claim: Through traffic mixed with walkers and dam visitors, producing congestion on the crossing and its approaches.
evidence.quote: Through traffic on US 93 combined with pedestrian and tourist traffic at Hoover Dam itself led to major traffic congestion on the dam and on the approaches to the dam.

evidence.claim: The old approaches had hairpin turns on both sides of the river, with terrain limiting sightlines through curves. Officials had discussed an alternative crossing since the 1960s.
evidence.quote: The approaches featured hairpin turns on both the Nevada and Arizona sides of the dam, and the terrain caused limited sight distances around curves.

evidence.claim: Officials had discussed an alternative crossing since the 1960s.
evidence.quote: Officials first discussed the need for a new Colorado River crossing that would bypass the dam in the 1960s.

evidence.claim: The bypass opened on October 19, 2010, moving US 93 to a new crossing and leaving SR 172 on the old alignment.
evidence.quote: SR 172 was originally part of US 93. US 93 was rerouted onto the Hoover Dam Bypass when construction was completed on October 19, 2010 and the new state highway was designated over the old route.

evidence.claim: From the interstate interchange, turn onto the old Nevada Highway and continue east over Rough Summit toward Lakeview.
evidence.quote: Proceeding northward for only a few feet, it turns right onto the old Nevada Highway, the original route of US 93. From there, the route travels eastward, following the curvy mountainside over Rough Summit headed toward Hoover Dam.

evidence.claim: Beyond the checkpoint, the access road passes the memorial bridge plaza and visitor center, then crosses the dam into Arizona.
evidence.quote: While the state highway designation ends at this point, the Hoover Dam Access Road continues eastward, passing the Mike O'Callaghan–Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge Plaza, the Hoover Dam visitor center and then crosses the dam itself into Arizona.

evidence.claim: The public drive loops through a parking area and returns the way it came.
evidence.quote: However, it only runs a short distance in that state before looping through a new parking area at a helipad to return the way it came

evidence.claim: At the bridge, stairs and ramps connect the Nevada parking area to the pedestrian sidewalk.
evidence.quote: A parking area is provided near the bridge on the Nevada side at what was a staging area during construction. A set of stairs and disabled access ramps lead to the sidewalk across the bridge.

evidence.claim: The turnoff for the Lakeview scenic viewpoint comes after Rough Summit on the eastbound approach to Hoover Dam.
evidence.quote: From there, the route travels eastward, following the curvy mountainside over Rough Summit headed toward Hoover Dam. Shortly after passing the turnoff for the Lakeview scenic viewpoint

evidence.claim: Just beyond it, SR 172 ends before the reservation’s security checkpoint. The road itself continues as Hoover Dam Access Road, carrying visitors toward the bridge plaza and dam.
evidence.quote: just prior to a security checkpoint at the boundary with the Bureau of Reclamation's Hoover Dam Reservation. While the state highway designation ends at this point, the Hoover Dam Access Road continues eastward, passing the Mike O'Callaghan–Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge Plaza

evidence.claim: The bridge that took US 93 off the dam opened in 2010, removing hairpin turns and blind curves from the highway’s route.
evidence.quote: Opened in 2010, it was the key component of the Hoover Dam Bypass project, which rerouted US 93 from its previous routing along the top of Hoover Dam and removed several hairpin turns and blind curves from the route.

evidence.claim: Its concrete arch and columns support a steel roadway deck, a combination chosen to control cost and schedule while complementing the dam.
evidence.quote: The composite design, using concrete for the arch and columns with steel construction for the roadway deck, was selected for schedule and cost control while being aesthetically compatible with the Hoover Dam.

evidence.claim: The name honors Nevada governor Mike O’Callaghan and Pat Tillman, who left professional football for the Army and was killed by friendly fire in Afghanistan.
evidence.quote: It is jointly named for Mike O'Callaghan, Governor of Nevada from 1971 to 1979, and Pat Tillman, an American football player who left his career with the Arizona Cardinals to enlist in the United States Army and was killed in Afghanistan by friendly fire in 2004.

evidence.claim: The distinction for visitors is between driving and walking: the dam is not visible from vehicles crossing the bridge, but its sidewalk provides views of the dam and river.
evidence.quote: Pedestrian access is provided over the bridge to tourists who wish to take in a different view of the nearby dam and river below, but the dam is not visible for those driving across it.

evidence.claim: Hoover Dam’s curved concrete face transfers the force of the stored water into the canyon walls.
evidence.quote: The curving arch of the dam would transmit the water's force into the abutments, in this case the rock walls of the canyon.

evidence.claim: Six Companies began construction in 1931, and the federal government accepted the dam in March 1936, more than two years ahead of schedule.
evidence.quote: The winning bid to build the dam was submitted by a consortium named Six Companies, Inc., which began construction in early 1931.

evidence.claim: Six Companies began construction in 1931, and the federal government accepted the dam in March 1936, more than two years ahead of schedule.
evidence.quote: the dam was turned over to the federal government on March 1, 1936, more than two years ahead of schedule.

evidence.claim: The concrete was poured in blocks with cooling pipes inside them; after each block stopped contracting, workers filled the pipes with grout.
evidence.quote: When an individual block had cured and had stopped contracting, the pipes were filled with grout.

evidence.claim: The concrete was poured in blocks with cooling pipes inside them
evidence.quote: concrete blocks in columns were poured

evidence.claim: with cooling pipes inside them
evidence.quote: Each five-foot form contained a set of 1-inch (25 mm) steel pipes; cool river water would be poured through the pipes, followed by ice-cold water from a refrigeration plant.

evidence.claim: Architect Gordon B. Kaufmann gave the project its Art Deco treatment, including turrets rising from the dam face and clocks on the intake towers.
evidence.quote: Kaufmann greatly streamlined the design and applied an elegant Art Deco style to the entire project. He designed sculpted turrets rising seamlessly from the dam face and clock faces on the intake towers

evidence.claim: Two traffic lanes cross the top, where US 93 formerly crossed the river.
evidence.quote: There are two lanes for automobile traffic across the top of the dam, which formerly served as the Colorado River crossing for U.S. Route 93.
